## What this is

My notes on [`prove-it`](https://github.com/specstoryai/hardcore-agentic-engineering),
the practice harness for Hardcore Agentic Engineering — a small TypeScript agent
loop with a gate at the exit.

Every output on this site is **executed at render time**, not pasted. If a claim
here is wrong, the page fails to build. That is the harness's own discipline
turned on my notes about it.

## The idea in one paragraph

An agent writes the code, writes the test, runs the test, reads the output, and
reports the result. Every link in the evidence chain routes through the party
being judged. `prove-it` answers that with a split enforced by directory:
`working/` is the only place worker tools can write, and `control/` is
host-owned — the gate, its signing key, the contracts, the receipts. A run
completes only when `dr-gate` reruns the agreed checks **itself** and signs a
receipt.

The worker's "done" is an opinion. Only the gate records completion.

## Command reference

The harness surface, and what each command touches.

| Command | Owner | What it does | Writes / edits |
|---|---|---|---|
| `loop open --run-id X` | worker side | Pins identities before any work | `runs/X/run.json`, `runs/X/events.jsonl` |
| `loop run --provider smoke --run-id X` | worker side | `open`, then drives the agent's turns | the above, plus `working/src/slugify.mjs` |
| `loop resume X` | worker side | Continues an interrupted run from the log | appends events; edits `working/` |
| `loop cancel X --reason "…"` | worker side | Ends a run deliberately | appends `run.cancelled` |
| `loop view X [--full]` | worker side | Folds the event log into a status | **nothing** |
| `loop complete X` | worker side | Asks the gate to verify, then records | appends `gate.result`, `run.completed` |
| **`dr-gate check X`** | **control** | **The judgment** — reruns the checks, signs | `runs/X/check-output.txt`, `control/receipts/X.json` |
| **`dr-gate verify X`** | **control** | **Re-validation** of an existing receipt | **nothing — read-only** |

`check` produces the verdict and is the only command that runs your check
command. `verify` runs nothing and re-reads a receipt. `complete` never judges
anything itself — it shells out to `dr-gate verify` and acts on the answer.

## The refusals

A gate is worth exactly what it refuses.

| Attack | Refusal |
|---|---|
| Alter the signature | `receipt not issued by this gate: signature does not verify` |
| Change the code after signing | `receipt stale: candidate tree mismatch` |
| Edit the contract after `open` | `contract hash mismatch: contract changed after the run was opened` |
| Reuse a valid receipt on another run | `receipt run mismatch: replay of run '…'` |
| Edit a pinned file | `protected check target modified: …` |
| Muzzle a check command | `suppressed check: '…' in '…'` |

The fourth is the one worth remembering: the signature verifies perfectly — the
payload is genuine — and it still refuses, because the run identity is wrong.
**A true receipt can still be the wrong receipt.**

## What a receipt does *not* say

> These named checks, run by the gate itself, against this exact tree, with
> these protected files byte-identical to `open`, under these exact contract
> bytes, produced these exit codes.

That is the whole claim. It says nothing about whether the checks were
*adequate*, and no mechanism anywhere in the system does. That gap is the course.

Two consequences I keep having to relearn:

1. **`protect` has teeth; `must_not_change` is a comment.** The gate parses
   `must_not_change` and never reads it again. On my own repository there is no
   fixture manifest, so `protect:` is the only mechanism with force.
2. **A check never seen red is not a check.** Run it against known-broken code
   and watch it fail before trusting it green. Reading the command cannot tell
   you the difference.
